investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or no free VM slots), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-carrying nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~140–147 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota is exhausted on both eligible nodes — all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods.

[Possible] The 2 kata-capable nodes are under resource pressure (CPU, memory, or extended resource limits) due to a recent workload increase, reducing available VM slots to zero.
[Lower confidence] A cluster scaling event or node failure reduced the number of kata-capable nodes from a previously higher count, shrinking total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below current demand.

investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents Swarm runtime has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots across all eligible nodes. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new peer-pod: 2 nodes had Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable (no preemption victims found on the 2 eligible nodes). This prevented the eval probe from creating the remote agent VM that is the prerequisite for all downstream state polling, causing all three remote-agents checks to time out unscheduled (~140–150 s each) and produce empty evidence payloads. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or no free VM slots), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-carrying nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~140–147 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota is exhausted on both eligible nodes — all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods.
[Likely] A surge or leak of remote agent pods that were not cleaned up has consumed all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, preventing new scheduling.

[Possible] The node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are simultaneously at capacity, creating a hard scheduling deadlock.
[Possible] The 2 kata-capable nodes are under resource pressure (CPU, memory, or extended resource limits) due to a recent workload increase, reducing available VM slots to zero.
[Lower confidence] A cluster scaling event or node failure reduced the number of kata-capable nodes from a previously higher count, shrinking total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below current demand.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 17:34 and 17:39 UTC on 2026-07-05 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes had 0 available slots for new remote agent pods, with 2 nodes reporting insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes failing pod affinity/selector matching. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected, causing a total contract gap against the remote-agent-runtime expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available cluster nodes: 2 nodes that match the kata.peerpods.io/vm node selector had insufficient remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable on both node groups. This prevented the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1918: createAgent with type "remote") from ever obtaining a running agent, so zero evidence was produced and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure failure caused by a runtime resource exhaustion condition in the production Kubernetes cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: the cluster's peer-pod VM quota on the 2 nodes that match the remote agent's node selector is fully consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for a new eval pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the remote agent pod's node affinity or selector rules, meaning only 2 nodes are even eligible, amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall on those 2 nodes (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Tertiary — cluster-wide resource pressure causing all eligible nodes to be at capacity simultaneously: a burst of concurrent remote agent workloads or other kata.peerpods.io/vm consumers may have saturated the 2 eligible nodes before the eval run began.

Lower confidence — eval scheduling contention: all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) ran sequentially and each independently hit the same scheduling wall, suggesting the condition was sustained for at least ~15 minutes (17:34–17:39 UTC), not a transient spike.

If leaked eval pods are found, terminate them to free kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and re-run the three failing remote-agents eval checks to confirm recovery.

Investigate whether the 4 nodes that failed affinity/selector matching are intentionally excluded from remote agent scheduling or whether a node label/taint change has inadvertently reduced the eligible node pool from a larger set to just 2.

Review the cluster's kata.peerpods.io/vm quota configuration to determine whether the current limit is sufficient for the expected concurrent load of eval probes plus production remote agent workloads, and consider increasing quota or adding eligible nodes if capacity is structurally insufficient.

Add a pre-flight eval check that verifies kata.peerpods.io/vm headroom on eligible nodes before attempting agent creation, so scheduling failures surface with a clearer diagnostic message rather than a raw Kubernetes scheduler error.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A subsequent eval run where the remote-agent-runtime pod schedules successfully and returns all 5 required evidence fields would disprove that the cluster is currently capacity-constrained.

kubectl output showing available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes would disprove resource exhaustion as the cause and point instead to a misconfiguration in the pod spec or scheduler.

Evidence that the 4 non-matching nodes were recently reconfigured to remove the required node labels or taints would shift the root cause from capacity exhaustion to a node affinity/selector regression.

A passing run of the sibling local-agent checks (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) at the same timestamp would confirm the failure is isolated to the remote/kata.peerpods.io/vm scheduling path and not a broader cluster or API outage.

Scheduler logs showing the pod was eventually scheduled but the eval runner timed out before it became Ready would shift the root cause from capacity exhaustion to an eval timeout threshold being too short.

Add a remote-agent-pod-leak check that counts pods in non-terminal states consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm and alerts if the count exceeds a configured threshold, catching resource leaks from prior eval runs before they block future scheduling.

Add a remote-agent-node-affinity check that verifies the expected number of nodes match the remote agent pod's node selector/affinity rules, alerting if the eligible node count drops below a minimum threshold.

Refine the remote-agent-runtime eval to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler reason (Unschedulable, resource type, node counts) as structured evidence fields so future failures are immediately machine-readable without log parsing.
